title: Private sandboxed tuning adviser and safe-apply pipeline
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Summary: Implement a private/VPC-capable automated tuning system that generates batching and KV-caching recommendations, verifies them in an air-gapped sandbox, and applies configuration changes with strong safety nets and policy enforcement. This work addresses customers who run Redwood Private in VPC/on‑prem environments where outbound telemetry is limited and org policies restrict automated changes.

Goals:
- Provide actionable batching/caching recommendations that maximize cost savings without violating latency SLOs or isolation requirements.
- Support an offline analysis mode that operates on local metrics/logs and synthetic workload traces.
- Add a sandboxed 'plan+verify' pipeline that executes proposed config changes in a constrained test environment before any production apply.
- Enforce org-level policies (max-batch-size, allowed quantizations, cache retention, RBAC) via a policy engine that blocks or annotates recommendations.
- Implement reversible safe-apply with time-limited rollbacks and automated post-apply verification checks.

Scope and constraints:
- Must work when control plane cannot reach Redwood hosted services; all analysis, policy checks, and sandbox runs must be possible within customer VPC or on-prem.
- Minimal default telemetry: operate using anonymized local metrics and sampled request traces; do not require raw PII or prompt data to leave customer network.
- Support integration points: KMS/HSM for key handling, local S3-compatible stores for sandbox artifacts, and private Prometheus push/gateway for metrics ingestion.

Design highlights and trade-offs:
- Offline analyzer: uses sliding-window token latency distributions, per-route tail latency, and historical throughput to compute estimated unit-cost delta for candidate batch sizes and cache TTLs. Trade-off: conservative bias recommended for private customers to avoid regressions; this reduces some potential savings.
- Sandbox executor: lightweight containerized harness that runs a short workload replay with a shadow pool of GPUs and artificially injected latency to validate tail behavior. Trade-off: requires customers to provision transient test capacity or allow small production traffic mirroring.
- Policy engine: declarative policies stored as YAML in customer git or config repo, evaluated locally before recommendations are presented. Trade-off: complexity for policy authors; we will provide a curated policy template set.
- Safe-apply: two-phase (plan -> staged apply -> automatic verification -> finalize) with automatic rollback if verification thresholds fail. Rollback uses cached previous config snapshot and a compensating control-plane command. Trade-off: rollout latency increases due to verification windows.

Acceptance criteria:
- Generate recommendations for batching and KV cache settings using only local telemetry for 3 sample Private customers (QA fixtures).
- Sandbox phase executes within customer network and produces a verification report within configured timeout (default 10 minutes).
- Policy engine blocks any recommendation that violates policy and produces human-readable rationale.
- Safe-apply can roll back within 5 minutes on a failing verification check in canary mode.
- End-to-end e2e test added to CI that runs the plan+sandbox+apply workflow against our simulated private cluster.

Artifacts and links:
- Design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/ENG/Private+Sandboxed+Tuning+Adviser
- Proto PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/4821
- Sandbox harness repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sandbox-harness (branch: private-safeapply)
- Policy templates: https://git.redwood.ai/private-policy-templates
- Dashboard for verification metrics: https://dash.redwood.ai/d/private-sandboxed-tuning/overview

Notes on security/compliance:
- Work with Security to validate that no sensitive prompt or customer PII is exfiltrated in offline analysis. Use deterministic hashing and aggregation.
- Ensure KMS integration supports HSM-backed operations for sandbox signing and rollback authorization.
- Provide audit logs of plan/apply/rollback events stored in customer-managed store for compliance retention.

Next steps:
1) Finalize policy schema and curated templates (owner: Security, due 2026-03-18).
2) Build offline analyzer prototype and validate on synthetic traces (owner: Ravi, due 2026-03-24).
3) Implement sandbox executor skeleton and runner (owner: QA infra, due 2026-03-31).
4) Security review and add HSM integration (owner: Security Eng, due 2026-03-26).
comments: 2026-03-10 Maya Chen: Kickoff meeting — aligned on offline-only mode and requirement to never send raw prompts off-network. Security raised KMS/HSM dependency.

2026-03-11 Ravi Singh: Prototype plan for analyzer using 95th/99th percentile latency windows; will default to conservative batch sizes for private customers. Posting initial metric extraction SQL in design doc.
2026-03-12 Elena Foster (Design): UX for the Console will show 'Sandboxed Preview' that includes expected cost delta, SLO risk score, and policy flags. Design spec link shared.
2026-03-13 Security review: flagged need for signed approvals for auto-apply in enterprise tier; added acceptance criterion for HSM-backed rollback signatures.

2026-03-14 Ravi Singh: Implemented analyzer shim that reads from Prometheus pushgateway; initial end-to-end smoke ran against local minikube cluster. Logs and sandbox artifacts stored in S3-compatible local store.
rollout_plan: Phase 0: internal QA with simulated private clusters (2 weeks). Phase 1: opt-in beta for 3 customers with dedicated sandbox capacity. Phase 2: gradual enable-by-policy for enterprise customers with audit logging and HSM signatures. Canary: 5% route traffic mirror then 25% then 100% if verification passes.
test_plan: Add unit tests for analyzer heuristics, integration tests for sandbox executor, and e2e test that runs plan+sandbox+apply+rollback against a simulated private environment. Performance targets: sandbox verification < 10 minutes; rollback < 5 minutes.
implementation_notes: Prefer pluggable connectors: prom/pushgateway, local S3, and a sandbox runner implemented in Kubernetes jobs. Keep default recommendations conservative (<= 0.8x tail latency increase budget). Provide 'aggressive' profile only under explicit allowlist policy.
